verses.text: Festus arrived in the province, and three days later he went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem.
There the leading priests and the most important Jewish leaders brought their charges against Paul. They begged Festus
to do them a favour and send Paul to Jerusalem. They were planning to hide and kill him on the way.
But Festus answered that Paul would be kept in Caesarea, and that he himself was going back there soon.
He said, "Let some of your leaders come with me. If this man has done anything wrong, they can accuse him there."
Festus stayed with them for more than ten days, and then he went down to Caesarea. The next day he sat in the judge's seat and ordered Paul to be brought in.
When Paul came in, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him. They brought many serious charges against him, but they could not prove any of them.
Paul defended himself and said, "I have done nothing wrong against the law of the Jews, or against the temple, or against Caesar."
But Festus wanted to please the Jews. So he asked Paul, "Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem and let me judge you there about these charges?"
Paul said, "I am standing before Caesar's court, and this is where I should be judged. I have done nothing wrong to the Jews, as you know very well.
If I have done wrong and deserve to die, I do not refuse to die. But if their charges against me are not true, no one can hand me over to them. I appeal to Caesar!"
Festus talked this over with his advisers. Then he said, "You have appealed to Caesar. To Caesar you will go!"
A few days later, King Agrippa and Bernice came to Caesarea to welcome Festus.
They stayed there many days, and Festus told the king about Paul's case. He said, "There is a man here whom Felix left in prison.
When I was in Jerusalem, the leading priests and the Jewish elders brought charges against him. They asked me to sentence him.
I told them that Romans do not hand over anyone before he has met his accusers face to face. He must have a chance to defend himself against their charges.
So when they came here, I did not waste any time. The next day I sat in the judge's seat and ordered the man to be brought in.
When his accusers stood up to speak, they did not accuse him of any of the crimes I expected.
Instead they argued with him about their own religion, and about a dead man named Jesus. Paul says that Jesus is alive.
I did not know how to look into these things. So I asked Paul if he would be willing to go to Jerusalem and be judged there about these charges.
But Paul asked to be kept in prison until the emperor could decide his case. So I ordered him to be kept until I could send him to Caesar."
Agrippa said to Festus, "I would like to hear this man myself." Festus answered, "Tomorrow you will hear him."
The next day Agrippa and Bernice came with great show. They went into the hall with the army commanders and the important men of the city. Then Festus ordered Paul to be brought in.
Festus said, "King Agrippa and everyone here with us, you see this man. All the Jews, here and in Jerusalem, have complained to me about him. They keep shouting that he should not live any longer.
But I found that he had done nothing that deserves death. And because he appealed to the emperor, I decided to send him.

But I have nothing definite to write to my lord about him. So I have brought him before all of you, and especially before you, King Agrippa. After we question him, I hope I will have something to write.
It makes no sense to me to send a prisoner without saying what the charges against him are."
